sanskrit: indram mitraṁ varuṇam agnim ūtaye mārutaṁ śardho aditiṁ havāmahe | rathaṁ na durgād vasavaḥ sudānavo viśvasmān no aṁhaso niṣ pipartana ||
english: We invoke Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni for our aid, the host of the Maruts, and Aditi. O Vasus, bounteous givers, like a chariot from a difficult pass, deliver us from every distress.

sanskrit: ta ādityā ā gatā sarvatātaye bhūta devā vṛtratūryeṣu śambhuvaḥ | rathaṁ na durgād vasavaḥ sudānavo viśvasmān no aṁhaso niṣ pipartana ||
english: Come hither, O Ādityas, for our complete welfare; be gracious, O gods, in the conquests of Vṛtra. O Vasus, bounteous givers, like a chariot from a difficult pass, deliver us from every distress.

sanskrit: avantu naḥ pitaraḥ supravācanā uta devī devapūtre ṛtāvṛdhā | rathaṁ na durgād vasavaḥ sudānavo viśvasmān no aṁhaso niṣ pipartana ||
english: May the Fathers, easy to invoke with fair laudations, help us; and the two divine goddesses, daughters of the gods, who promote ṛta. O Vasus, bounteous givers, like a chariot from a difficult pass, deliver us from every distress.

sanskrit: narāśaṁsaṁ vājinaṁ vājayann iha kṣayadvīram pūṣaṇaṁ sumnair īmahe | rathaṁ na durgād vasavaḥ sudānavo viśvasmān no aṁhaso niṣ pipartana ||
english: We call hither with hymns of praise Narāśaṁsa the mighty, the lord of steeds who quickens prizes, Pūṣan, ruler of men. O Vasus, bounteous givers, like a chariot from a difficult pass, deliver us from every distress.

sanskrit: bṛhaspate sadam in naḥ sugaṁ kṛdhi śaṁ yor yat te manurhitaṁ tad īmahe | rathaṁ na durgād vasavaḥ sudānavo viśvasmān no aṁhaso niṣ pipartana ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, make our path ever easy; we seek that blessing and prosperity which Manu established for you. O Vasus, bounteous givers, like a chariot from a difficult pass, deliver us from every distress.

sanskrit: indraṁ kutso vṛtrahaṇaṁ śacīpatiṁ kāṭe nibāḷha ṛṣir ahvad ūtaye | rathaṁ na durgād vasavaḥ sudānavo viśvasmān no aṁhaso niṣ pipartana ||
english: The sage Kutsa, hemmed in a ravine, called Indra, the Vṛtra-slayer, lord of might, for his aid. O Vasus, bounteous givers, like a chariot from a difficult pass, deliver us from every distress.

sanskrit: devair no devy aditir ni pātu devas trātā trāyatām aprayucchan | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: May divine Aditi with the gods protect us; may the divine Protector guard us without slackening. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: yajño devānāṁ praty eti sumnam ādityāso bhavatā mṛḻayantaḥ | ā vo 'rvācī sumatirvavṛtyād aṁhoś cid yā varivovittarāsat ||
english: The sacrifice returns gracious favour from the gods; O Ādityas, be merciful to us. May your benevolent thought be turned hither toward us — that which is most spacious even amid distress.

sanskrit: upa no devā avasā gamantu aṅgirasāṁ sāmabhiḥ stūyamānāḥ | indra indriyair marutaḥ marudbhir ādityair no aditiḥ śarma yaṁsat ||
english: May the gods come to us with aid, praised with the hymns of the Aṅgirasas. May Indra with his powers, the Maruts with their troop, and Aditi with the Ādityas bestow shelter on us.

sanskrit: tan na indras tad varuṇas tad agnis tad aryamā tat savitā cano dhāt | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: May Indra, Varuṇa, Agni, Aryaman, and Savitṛ bestow that delight upon us. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: ya indrāgnī citratamoratho vām abhi viśvāni bhuvanāni caṣṭe | tenā yātaṁ sarathaṁ tasthivāṁsā athā somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: That most brilliant chariot of yours, O Indrāgnī, which surveys all the worlds — come riding together in that very chariot, and drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yāvad idaṁ bhuvanaṁ viśvam asty uruvyacā varimatā gabhīram | tāvāṁ ayaṁ pātave somo astv aram indrāgnī manase yuvabhyām ||
english: As vast as all this world extends, wide-spreading and deep in its expanse — let this Soma be ready for you both to drink, O Indrāgnī, fitting for your minds.

sanskrit: cakrethe hi sadhriyaṅ nāma bhadraṁ sadhrīcīnā vṛtrahaNā uta sthaḥ | tāv indrāgnī sadhrya-ñcā niṣadyā vṛṣṇaḥ somasya vṛṣaṇā vṛṣethām ||
english: For you have established the auspicious name Sadhrīya; you are both Sadhrīcīna and Vṛtra-slayers. Sit together, O Indrāgnī, and drink deep of the bull Soma, you mighty ones.

sanskrit: samiddheṣv agniṣv ānajānā yatasrucā barhir u tistirāṇā | tīvraiḥ somai pariṣiktebhir arvāg endrāgnī saumanasāya yātam ||
english: When the fires are kindled and the ladles are held ready, and the sacred grass is spread — come hither, O Indrāgnī, with the poured, potent Soma offerings, for our well-being.

sanskrit: yānīndrāgnī cakrethur vīryāṇi yāni rūpāṇy uta vṛṣṇyāni | yā vāṁ pratnāni sakhyā śivāni tebhiḥ somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: The heroic deeds and the forms and the manly powers that you two, O Indrāgnī, have performed, and those ancient friendships that are auspicious between you — with those qualities, drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yad abravam prathamaṁ vāṁ vṛṇāno 'yaṁ somo asurair no vivhavyaḥ | tāṁ satyāṁ śraddhām abhy ā hi yātam athā somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: I first declared my desire for you both: this Soma of ours calls you here, not the Asuras. Come hither to that true faith, and then drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yad indrāgnī madhataḥ sve duroṇe yad brahmaṇi rājani vā yajatrā | ataḥ pari vṛṣaṇāv ā hi yātam athā somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: Whether you two, O Indrāgnī, are revelling in your own house, or among the brahman, or in the royal hall, O adorable ones — come hither from there, you mighty ones, and drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yad indrāgnī yaduṣu turvaśeṣu yad druhyuṣv anuṣu pūruṣu sthaḥ | ataḥ pari vṛṣaṇāv ā hi yātam athā somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: Whether you two, O Indrāgnī, are among the Yadus and Turvaśas, or among the Druhyus, Anus, and Pūrus — come hither from there, you mighty ones, and drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yad indrāgnī avamasyāṁ pṛthivyāṁ madhyamasyāṁ paramasyāṁ uta sthaḥ | ataḥ pari vṛṣaṇāv ā hi yātam athā somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: Whether you two, O Indrāgnī, are on the lowest earth, the middle, or the highest — come hither from there, you mighty ones, and drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yad indrāgnī paramasyāṁ pṛthivyāṁ madhyamasyāṁ avamasyāṁ uta sthaḥ | ataḥ pari vṛṣaṇāv ā hi yātam athā somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: Whether you two, O Indrāgnī, are on the highest earth, the middle, or the lowest — come hither from there, you mighty ones, and drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yad indrāgnī divi ṣṭho yat pṛthivyāṁ yat parvateṣv oṣadhīṣv apsu | ataḥ pari vṛṣaṇāv ā hi yātam athā somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: Whether you two, O Indrāgnī, are in heaven, on earth, in the mountains, among the plants, or in the waters — come hither from there, you mighty ones, and drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: yad indrāgnī uditā sūryasya madhye divaḥ svadhayā mādayethe | ataḥ pari vṛṣaṇāv ā hi yātam athā somasya pibataṁ sutasya ||
english: Whether you two, O Indrāgnī, take delight of your own accord at the rising of the sun, in the midst of heaven — come hither from there, you mighty ones, and drink of the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: evendrāgnī papivāṁsā sutasya viśvāsmabhyaṁ saṁ jayataṁ dhanāni | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Even so, O Indrāgnī, having drunk of the pressed Soma, win all riches for us. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: vi hy akhyam manasā vasya icchann indrāgnī jñāsa uta vā sajātān | nānyā yuvat pramatirastī mahyaṁ sa vāṁ dhiyaṁ vājayantīm atakṣam ||
english: I have looked about with the mind seeking better things — O Indrāgnī, I would know you, or else the kinsmen. No other guardian is mine but you; I have fashioned for you both this thought that wins the prize.

sanskrit: aśravaṁ hi bhūridāvattarā vāṁ vijāmātur uta vā ghā syālāt | athā somasya prayatī yuvabhyām indrāgnī stomaṁ janayāmi navyam ||
english: I have heard that you both are more lavishly giving than a maternal uncle or a brother-in-law. And so, as the Soma is offered to you both, O Indrāgnī, I create a fresh hymn of praise.

sanskrit: mā cchedma raśmīṁr iti nādhamānāḥ pitṝṇāṁ śaktīr anuyacchamānāḥ | indrāgnibhyāṁ kaṁ vṛṣaṇo madanti tā hy adrī dhiṣaṇāyā upasthe ||
english: Imploring, let us not sever the cords nor withdraw the ancestral powers. What mighty ones rejoice in both Indra and Agni? — truly the two pressing stones in the lap of Dhiṣaṇā.

sanskrit: yuvābhyāṁ devī dhiṣaṇā madāyendrāgnī somam uśatī sunoti | tāv aśvinā bhadrahastā supāṇī ā dhāvatam madhunā pṛṅktam apsu ||
english: For your delight, O Indrāgnī, the divine Dhiṣaṇā, full of eagerness, presses the Soma. Come, you with auspicious hands and beautiful fingers like the Aśvins — hasten and mingle it with honey in the waters.

sanskrit: yuvām indrāgnī vasuno vibhāge tavastamā śuśrava vṛtrahatye | tāv āsadyā barhiṣi yajñe asmin pra carṣaṇī mādayethāṁ sutasya ||
english: You two, O Indrāgnī, most mighty ones, are heard of in the division of riches and in the slaying of Vṛtra. Seat yourselves on the sacred grass at this sacrifice and, O ye champions of men, exhilarate yourselves with the pressed Soma.

sanskrit: pra carṣaṇibhyaḥ pṛtanāhaveṣu pra pṛthivyā riricāthe divaś ca | pra sindhumhyaḥ pra giribhyo mahitvā prendrāgnī viśvā bhuvanāty anyā ||
english: You two excel all men in the contests of battle; you exceed both earth and heaven; you surpass the rivers and mountains in greatness. O Indrāgnī, you two surpass all other beings.

sanskrit: ā bharataṁ śikṣataṁ vajrabāhū asmāṁ indrāgnī avataṁ śacībhiḥ | ime nu te raśmayaḥ sūryasya yebhiḥ sapitvam pitaro na āsan ||
english: Bring your gifts, O you wielders of the thunderbolt; protect us, O Indrāgnī, with your powers. These rays of the sun by which our fathers had communion with you — may they be ours.

sanskrit: puraṁdarā śikṣataṁ vajrahastā asmāṁ indrāgnī avataṁ bhareṣu | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: O breakers of forts with thunderbolt in hand, protect us, O Indrāgnī, in battles. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: tatam me apas tad u tāyate punaḥ svādiṣṭhā dhītir ucathāya śasyate | ayaṁ samudra iha viśvadebyaḥ svāhākṛtasya saṁ u tṛpṇuta ṛbhavaḥ ||
english: My work is spread out, and it spreads anew; the sweetest thought is proclaimed for praise. This ocean here belongs to all the gods — O Ṛbhus, be satisfied with what has been hallowed with svāhā.

sanskrit: ābhogayam pra yad icchanta aitanāpākāḥ prāñco mama ke cid āpayaḥ | saudhanvanāsaś caritasya bhūmanāgacchata saviturdāśuṣo gṛham ||
english: When you went forth seeking enjoyment, O you who came from afar, proceeding eastward, O Saudhanvanā Ṛbhus — having traversed all the regions of your journey, come to the home of the generous Savitṛ.

sanskrit: tat savitā vo amṛtatvam āsuvad agohyaṁ yac chrāvayanta aitana | tyaṁ cic camasam asurasya bhakṣaṇam ekaṁ santam akṛṇutā caturvayam ||
english: Savitṛ has impelled for you that immortality which, when you went forth, was proclaimed as indestructible. That single cup used by the Asura for drinking you made into four.

sanskrit: viṣṭvī śamī taraṇitvena vāghato martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ | saudhanvanā ṛbhavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ saṁvatsare saṁ apṛcyanta dhītibhiḥ ||
english: Having peacefully settled through their skill of swift crossing, these mortals, being mortal, attained to immortality. The Saudhanvanā Ṛbhus, bright-eyed as the sun, were united throughout the year with their devotional works.

sanskrit: kṣetram iva vi mamus tejanenaṁ ekaṁ pātraṁ ṛbhavo jehamānam | upastutā upamaṁ nādhamānā amartyeṣu śrava icchamānāḥ ||
english: Like a field they measured out the wobbling single cup with precision, O Ṛbhus. Praised and most worthy of praise, imploring, they sought renown among the immortals.

sanskrit: ā manīṣām antarikṣasya nṛbhyaḥ sruceva ghṛtaṁ juhavāma vidmanā | taraṇitvā ye pitur asya saścira ṛbhavo vājam aruhan divo rajaḥ ||
english: Let us pour thought to the men of the mid-air like ghee poured into the ladle, with knowledge. The Ṛbhus, who by their swift skill followed their father, mounted to the realm of heaven for the prize.

sanskrit: ṛbhur na indraḥ śavasā navīyān ṛbhur vājebhir vasubhir vasur dadiḥ | yuṣmākaṁ devā avasāhani priye abhi tiṣṭhema pṛtsutyīr asunvatām ||
english: Indra is like an Ṛbhu, ever renewed in strength; the Ṛbhu gives wealth with prizes and good things. By your aid, O gods, on that beloved day of victory, may we prevail over the armies of those who press no Soma.

sanskrit: niś carmaṇa ṛbhavo gām apiṁśata saṁ vatsenāsṛjatā mātaram punaḥ | saudhanvanāsaḥ svapasyayā naro jīvrī yuvānā pitarākṛṇotana ||
english: The Ṛbhus fashioned a cow from the hide; they reunited the calf with its mother. O Saudhanvanā Ṛbhus, by your wonderful skill, you, O men, made your two parents — decrepit and aged — young again.

sanskrit: vājebhir no vājasātāv aviḍḍhy ṛbhumāṁ indra citram ā darṣi rādhaḥ | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Help us, O Indra, rich in prizes, to win wealth in the contest of prizes; show forth your wondrous bounty, O Ṛbhavan. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: takṣan rathaṁ suvṛtaṁ vidmanāpasas takṣan harī indrāvāhā vṛṣaṇvasū | takṣan pitṛbhyām ṛbhavo yuvad vayas takṣan vatsāya mātaraṁ sacābhuvam ||
english: The skilful ones fashioned a chariot with good wheels; they fashioned the two bay horses, bearers of Indra, rich in might. The Ṛbhus fashioned youthful vigour for the parents; they fashioned the cow who stays with her calf.

sanskrit: ā no yajñāya takṣata ṛbhumad vayaḥ kratve dakṣāya suprajāvatīm iṣam | yathā kṣayāma sarvavīrayā viśā tan naḥ śardhāya dhāsathā sv indriyam ||
english: Fashion for our sacrifice a Ṛbhu-like vigour, for wisdom and skill, a food-supply with fine offspring, so that we may dwell with all our people in heroic strength. Bestow on us complete Indra-power.

sanskrit: ā takṣata sātiṁ asmabhyam ṛbhavaḥ sātiṁ rathāya sātiṁ arvate naraḥ | sātiṁ no jaitrīṁ sam maheta viśvahā jāmim ajāmiṁ pṛtanāsu sakṣaṇim ||
english: Fashion a prize for us, O Ṛbhus; a prize for the chariot, a prize for the steed, O men. Magnify our prize that ever conquers, kin or unkin, victorious in battles.

sanskrit: ṛbhukṣaṇam indram ā huva ūtaya ṛbhūn vājān marutaḥ somapītaye | ubhā mitrāvaruṇā nūnam aśvinā te no hinvantu sātaye dhiye jiṣe ||
english: I call Indra-Ṛbhukṣan for aid, and the Ṛbhus and Vājas, and the Maruts, for the drinking of Soma. May both Mitra-Varuṇa and now the Aśvins spur us on to win the prize, for thought and for victory.

sanskrit: ṛbhur bharāya saṁ śiśātu sātiṁ samaryajid vājo asmāṁ aviṣṭu | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: May Ṛbhu sharpen the prize for the contest; may Vāja, the battle-winner, assist us. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: īḷe dyāvāpṛthivī pūrvacittaye agniṁ gharmaṁ surucaṁ yāmann iṣṭaye | yābhir bhare kāram aṁśāya jinvathas tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: I invoke Heaven and Earth for prior wisdom, and Agni the warmth, the bright one, on our journey for worship. With those aids by which you quicken the pressing of the prize-portion, O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yuvor dānāya subharā asaścato ratham ā tasthur vacasaṁ na mantave | yābhir dhiyo avathaḥ karmann iṣṭaye tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: The never-failing, easy-carrying ones mounted the chariot for your gift, as if to reach a spoken word. With those aids by which you protect devotions for the worship-rite, O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ tāsāṁ divyasya praśāsane viśāṁ kṣayatho amṛtasya majmanā | yābhir dhenuṁ aśvam pinvatho narā tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: You two rule over those celestial beings under heaven's governance, by virtue of the great immortal realm. With those aids by which you swell the milk-cow and the horse, O men, O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ parijmā tanayasya majmanā dvimātā tūrṣu taraṇir vibhūṣati | yābhis trimantus abhavad vicakṣaṇas tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which the All-surrounding One glorifies the full greatness of his son who has two mothers, swift and rushing; with those by which Trimanta became discerning — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhīr rebhaṁ nivṛtaṁ sitam adbhya ud vandanam airayataṁ svar dṛśe | yābhiḥ kaṇvam pra siṣāsantam āvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you raised up Rebha, sunken and buried under the waters, to see the light of day; with those aids by which you helped Kaṇva who was striving forward — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhir antakaṁ jasamānam āraṇe bhujyuṁ yābhir avyathibhir jijinvathuḥ | yābhiḥ karkandhum vayyaṁ ca jinvathas tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you sustained Antaka who was dying in a distant place, and Bhujyu without wavering; with those by which you quickened Karkandhu and Vayya — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ śucantim dhanasāṁ suṣaṁsadam taptaṁ gharmam omyāvantam atraye | yābhiḥ pṛśnigum purukutsam āvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you helped Śucanti, the prize-seeker, who sits securely, and by which the burning warmth came with shelter for Atri; with those by which you aided Pṛśnigu and Purukutsa — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ śacībhir vṛṣaṇā parāvṛjam prāndhaṁ śroṇaṁ cakṣasa etave kṛthaḥ | yābhir vartikāṁ grasitām amuñcataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those powerful aids, O mighty ones, by which you enabled the blind and lame to go away and see; with those by which you freed the quail that had been swallowed — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ sindhum madhumantam asaścataṁ vasiṣṭhaṁ yābhir ajarāv ajinvatam | yābhiḥ kutsaṁ śrutaryaṁ naryam āvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which, never-failing, you quickened the honeyed Sindhū and Vasiṣṭha, you two undecaying ones; with those by which you aided Kutsa, the glorious and manly one — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhir viśpalāṁ dhanasām atharvaṁ sahasramīḷha ājāv ajinvatam | yābhir vaśam aśvyam preṇim āvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which, with a thousand rewards, you quickened Viśpalā the prize-seeker, the Atharvan, in the battle; with those by which you aided Vaśa, the horse-owner Preṇi — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ sudānū auśijāya vaṇije dīrghaśravase madhu kośo akṣarat | kakṣīvantaṁ stotāraṁ yābhir āvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which, for the merchant Auśija Dīrghaśravas, the honey-vessel overflowed, O bounteous ones; with those by which you aided Kakṣīvant the praiser — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhī rasāṁ kṣodasodnaḥ pipinvathu ranāśvaṁ yābhī ratham āvataṁ jiṣe | yābhis triśoka usriyā udājata tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you filled the Rasā, whose waters are sweet as milk; with those by which you helped the horseless chariot to victory; with those by which Triśoka drove forth the dawn-cows — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ sūryam pariyāthaḥ parāvati mandhātāraṁ kṣaitrapatyeṣv āvataṁ | yābhir vipram pra bharadvājam āvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you go around the sun in the far distance; with those by which you aided Mandhātṛ in the lordship of his field; with those by which you aided the inspired Bharadvāja — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhir mahām atithigvaṁ kaśojuvaṁ divodāsaṁ śambara-hatya āvataṁ | yābhiḥ pūrbhidye trasadasyu māvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you helped the great Atithigva Kaśojuva, Divodāsa, in the slaying of Śambara; with those by which you aided Trasadasyu in the breaking of forts — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhir vaṁraṁ vipipānam upastutaṁ kaliṁ yābhir vittajāniṁ duvasyathaḥ | yābhir vyaśvam uta pṛthim āvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you honour Vaṁra, sorely afflicted and already praised; and the blind Kali who has lost his wealth; with those by which you aided Vyaśva and Pṛthi — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhir narā śayave yābhir atraye yābhiḥ purā manave gātum īṣathuḥ | yābhiḥ śārīr ājataṁ syūmaraśmaye tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which, O men, you helped Śaya and Atri, and formerly showed the way to Manu; with those by which you drove the chariot of Śārī with Syūmaraśmi — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ paṭharvā jaṭharasya majmanā agnir nādīdec cita iddho ajmann ā | yābhiḥ śaryātam avattho mahādhane tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which — through the greatness of Jaṭhara's belly — the fire blazed forth clearly, kindled on the march; with those by which you aided Śaryāta in a great prize contest — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhir aṅgiro manasā niranyatho 'graṁ gacchatho vivare goarṇasaḥ | yābhir manuṁ śūram iṣā samāvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you freed Aṅgiras by mind, going to the forefront in the opening of the cow-pen; with those by which you aided the heroic Manu with food in battle — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ patnīr vimadāya nyūhathu ā gha vā yābhir aruṇīr aśikṣatam | yābhiḥ sudāsa ūhathuḥ sudevyaṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you brought brides to Vimada; and those by which you indeed gave instruction to the Aruṇīs; with those by which you carried pious Sudāsa to divine bliss — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ śaṁtātī bhavatho dadāśuṣe bhujyuṁ yābhir avattho yābhir adhrigum | omyāvatīṁ subharāṁ ṛtastubhaṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you become beneficent for the worshipper, and aided Bhujyu; and those by which you aided Adhrigu, the bearer of shelter and abundance, who praises ṛta — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ kṛśānum asane duvasyatho jave yābhir yūno arvantam āvataṁ | madhu priyaṁ bharatho yat saraḍbhyas tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you honour Kṛśānu in the contest for the prize; with those by which you aided the young man's swift horse; and with those by which you bring sweet honey for the bees — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhir naraṁ goṣuyudhaṁ nṛṣāhye kṣetrasya sātā tanayasya jinvathaḥ | yābhī rathāṁ avatho yābhir arvatas tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids by which you quicken the man who fights for cows, in the battle of heroes, for the winning of a field and a son; with those by which you aid chariots and horses — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ kutsam ārjuneyaṁ śatakratū pra turvītiṁ pra ca dabhītiṁ āvataṁ | yābhir dhvasantiṁ puruṣantiṁ āvataṁ tābhir ū ṣu ūtibhir aśvinā gatam ||
english: With those aids, O you of a hundred powers, by which you aided Kutsa the son of Arjuna, and Turvīti and Dabhīti; with those by which you aided Dhvasanti and Puruṣanti — O Aśvins, come with those aids.

sanskrit: apnasvantīm aśvinā vācam asme kṛtaṁ no dasrā vṛṣaṇā manīṣām | adyūtye 'vase ni hvaye vāṁ vṛdhe ca no bhavataṁ vājasātau ||
english: Grant us, O Aśvins, a speech bearing good results; fashion our prayer, O wonderful ones, O mighty ones. I call upon you today for aid and to increase us; be with us for the winning of prizes.

sanskrit: dyubhir aktubhiḥ pari pātam asmān ariṣṭebhir aśvinā saubhāgebhiḥ | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Guard us by day and by night with auspicious, bountiful protections, O Aśvins. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: idaṁ śreṣṭhaṁ jyotiṣāṁ jyotir āgāc citraḥ praketho ajaniṣṭa vibhvā | yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāyam̐ evā rātry uṣase yonim āraik ||
english: This best light among lights has come; the bright discernment was born far-shining. As prompted by Savitṛ for his sending forth, even so Night has yielded her station to Dawn.

sanskrit: ruśadvatsā ruśatī śvetyāgād āraig u kṛṣṇā sadanāny asyāḥ | samānabandhu amṛte anūcī dyāvā varṇaṁ carata āminā ne ||
english: She has come, the bright one with her bright offspring, having put to flight the Dark One from her dwelling-places. Immortal sisters, moving together in turn, Heaven and Dawn exchange their colours at the dawn.

sanskrit: samāno adhvā svasor anantas tam anyānyā carato devaśiṣṭe | na methete na tasthatuḥ sumeke naktoṣāsā samanasā virūpe ||
english: The common path of the two sisters is endless; they walk it, each in turn, taught by the gods. They do not collide, nor do they stand still; harmonious though different in form, Night and Dawn move together in one mind.

sanskrit: bhāsvatī netrī sūnṛtānām aceti citrā vi duro na āvaḥ | prārpyā jagad vy u no rāyo akhyad uṣā ajīgar bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: The bright leader of glad tidings has appeared; the brilliant one has opened the doors for us. Setting the world in motion, she has revealed riches to us — Dawn has awakened all the worlds.

sanskrit: jihmaśye caritave maghony ābhogaya iṣṭaye rāya u tvam | dabhrham paśyadbhya urviyā vicakṣa uṣā ajīgar bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: O bountiful one, you cause movement for those who lie crooked, and stir to seek and enjoy riches. You show your broad radiance for those who see little — Dawn has awakened all the worlds.

sanskrit: kṣatrāya tvam śravase tvam mahīyā iṣṭaye tvam artham iva tvam ityai | visadṛśā jīvitābhipracakṣa uṣā ajīgar bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: For sovereignty are you, for glory you are great; for worship and as the very goal of effort do you come. You reveal the varied spectacle of living beings — Dawn has awakened all the worlds.

sanskrit: eṣā divo duhitā praty adarśi vyucchantī yuvatiḥ śukravāsāḥ | viśvasyeśānā pārthavasya vasva uṣo adyeha subhage vy uccha ||
english: She has appeared, the daughter of heaven, the young maiden, shining forth in bright garments. Mistress of all earthly wealth — O Uṣas, shine forth here today, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: parāyatīnām anv eti pātham āyatīnāṁ prathamā śaśvatīnām | vyucchantī jīvam udīrayantī uṣā mṛtaṁ kaṁ ca na bodhayanntī ||
english: She follows the path of those that have gone before, and is the first among the countless ones yet to come. She, the Dawn, shining forth, stirs the living to action; she wakens no one who is dead.

sanskrit: uṣo yad agniṁ samidhe cakartha vi yad āvaś cakṣasā sūryasya | yan mānuṣān yakṣyamāṇāṁ ajīgas tad deveṣu cakṛṣe bhadram apnaḥ ||
english: O Uṣas, when you kindled the fire, when you unveiled with the eye of the sun, when you stirred men who would perform worship — thereby you have wrought auspicious gain among the gods.

sanskrit: kiyāty ā yat samayā bhavāti yā vyūṣur yāś ca nūnaṁ vyucchān | anu pūrvāḥ kṛpate vāvaśānā pradīdhyānā joṣam anyābhir eti ||
english: How many Dawns have already passed? And how many that are now shining? She longs after the earlier Dawns, calling eagerly; glowing she goes harmoniously with the others still to come.

sanskrit: īyuṣ ṭe ye pūrvataraṁ apaśyan vyucchantīm uṣasaṁ martyāsaḥ | asmābhir ū nu praticakṣyābhūd o te yanti ye aparīṣu paśyān ||
english: Those mortals have gone who saw the Dawn shining in the earlier time. Now she has come to be seen by us; those will come also who will see her in future times.

sanskrit: yāvayadveṣā ṛtapā ṛtejāḥ sumnāvarī sūnṛtā īrayantī | sumaṅgalīr bibhratī devavītiṁ ihādyoṣaḥ śreṣṭhatamā vy uccha ||
english: You who drive away hatred, who guard ṛta, who are born of ṛta, who confer bliss and send forth kind words, who bring the most auspicious gifts, who carry the divine feast — O Uṣas, shine forth here today as the most excellent.

sanskrit: śaśvat purośā vy uvāsa devy atho adyedaṁ vy āvo maghonī | atho vy ucchād uttarāṁ anu dyūn ajarāmṛtā carati svadhābhiḥ ||
english: Ever before has the divine Uṣas shone forth; and today again, she the bountiful one has shone. And she will yet shine forth for more days to come — she, immortal, ageless, moves by her own powers.

sanskrit: vy añjibhir diva ātāsv adyaud apa kṛṣṇāṁ nirṇijaṁ devy āvaḥ | prabodhayantī aruṇebhir aśvair oṣā yāti suyujā rathena ||
english: Lighting up the approaches of heaven with her rays, the divine one has driven away the black shroud. Awakening all, Dawn goes forth with her reddish horses, in her well-harnessed chariot.

sanskrit: āvahantī poṣyā vāryāṇi citraṁ ketuṁ kṛṇute cekitānā | īyuṣīṇām upamā śaśvatīnāṁ vibhātīnāṁ prathamoṣā vy aśvait ||
english: Bringing nourishing and desirable gifts, the knowing one makes a wondrous banner. The foremost of those that have passed, among the countless countless, among those that shine — Dawn has dawned first.

sanskrit: ud īrdhvaṁ jīvo asur na āgād apa prāgāt tama ā jyotir eti | āraik panthāṁ yātave sūryāyāganma yatra pratiranta āyuḥ ||
english: Rise up — the living breath has come to us; the darkness has departed; light is coming. She has opened the path for the sun to travel; we have arrived where life is prolonged.

sanskrit: syūmanā vāca ud iyarti vahniḥ stavāno rebha uṣaso vibhātīḥ | adyā tad uccha gṛṇate maghony asme āyur ni didīhi prajāvat ||
english: The singer, the bearer of the hymn, raises his voice with the stringing of words, praising the shining Dawns. Shine forth today that, O bountiful one; shine your offspring-bearing light of life upon us.

sanskrit: yā gomatīr uṣasaḥ sarvavīrā vyucchanti dāśuṣe martyāya | vāyor iva sūnṛtānām udarke tā aśvadā aśnavat somasutva ||
english: Those Dawns rich in cattle and in all heroes that shine forth for the mortal worshipper — as a surge of glad tidings like the wind — may he who presses Soma obtain those givers of horses.

sanskrit: mātā devānām aditir anīkaṁ yajñasya ketuṁ bṛhatī vi bhāhi | praśastikṛd brahmaṇe no vy ucchā no jane janaya viśvavāre ||
english: Aditi, mother of the gods, the banner of sacrifice, shine forth in your greatness. O you who confer renown, shine forth for the brahman among us; create offspring for our people, O you who hold all that is desirable.

sanskrit: yac citram apna uṣaso vahantī jānāya śaśamānāya bhadram | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: That wondrous good fortune which Dawn brings for the man who knows and strives — may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: imā rudrāya tavase kapardine kṣayadvīrāya pra bharāmahe matīḥ | yathā śam asad dvipade catuṣpade viśvam puṣṭaṁ grāme asmin anāturam ||
english: We offer these hymns to powerful Rudra of the braided hair, the ruler of heroes, so that all may be well with our bipeds and quadrupeds, so that all in this village may prosper and be free from disease.

sanskrit: mṛḻā no rudro uta no mayas kṛdhi kṣayadvīrāya namasā vidhema te | yac chaṁ ca yoś ca manur āyeje pitā tad aśyāma tava rudra praṇītiṣu ||
english: Be gracious to us, O Rudra, and bring us welfare; we would honour you with worship, O ruler of heroes. Whatever health and happiness Manu, our father, won through sacrifice — may we attain that under your guidance, O Rudra.

sanskrit: aśyāma te sumatim devayajyayā kṣayadvīrasya tava rudra mīḍhvaḥ | sumnāyann id viśo asmākam ā car ariṣṭavīrā juhavāma te haviḥ ||
english: May we attain your grace, O Rudra the shower of blessings, ruler of heroes, through worship of the deity. Come graciously to our people; with our heroes unhurt may we pour oblation to you.

sanskrit: tveṣaṁ vayam rudraṁ yajñasādham vaṅkuṁ kavim avase ni hvayāmahe | āre asmad daivyaṁ heḻo asyatu sumatim id vayam asyā vṛṇīmahe ||
english: We call hither for aid the impetuous Rudra, accomplisher of the sacrifice, the agile seer. Let his divine wrath be far from us; we choose only his benevolence.

sanskrit: divo varāham aruṣaṁ kapardinam tveṣaṁ rūpaṁ namasā ni hvayāmahe | haste bibhrad bheṣajā vāryāṇi śarma varma cchardi asmabhyaṁ yaṁsat ||
english: The red boar of heaven, of braided hair, of fearful form — we call upon with worship. May he, holding in his hand desirable healing herbs, bestow shelter, armour, and refuge upon us.

sanskrit: idam pitre marutām ucyate vacaḥ svādoḥ svādīyo rudrāya vardhanam | rāsvā ca no amṛta martabhojanaṁ tmane tokāya tanayāya mṛḻa ||
english: This word is spoken as praise and increase for Rudra, father of the Maruts, sweeter than the sweet. Grant to us, O immortal, what mortals may enjoy; be gracious to us, to our own selves, and to our children and their children.

sanskrit: mā no mahāntam uta mā no arbhakam mā na ukṣantam uta mā na ukṣitam | mā no vadhīḥ pitaram ota mātaraṁ mā naḥ priyās tanvo rudra rīriṣaḥ ||
english: Slay not our great one, nor our little one, not our growing youth, nor our grown man; slay not our father, nor our mother; harm not, O Rudra, any of those dear to us.

sanskrit: mā nas toke tanaye mā na āyau mā no goṣu mā no aśveṣu rīriṣaḥ | vīrān mā no rudra bhāmito vadhīr haviṣmantaḥ sadam it tvā havāmahe ||
english: Harm not our children or our children's children, nor our life, not our cows, not our horses; slay not our heroes in anger, O Rudra; we who bear oblations call upon you ever.

sanskrit: upa te stomān paśupā ivākaram rāsvā pitar marutāṁ sumnam asme | bhadrā hi te sumatir mṛḻayattamā athā vayam ava it te vṛṇīmahe ||
english: I have brought you praises as a herdsman brings his cattle; grant us your favour, O father of the Maruts. For your benevolence is auspicious and most merciful — therefore we choose only your grace.

sanskrit: āre te goghnam uta pūruṣaghnaṁ kṣayadvīra sumnam asme te astu | mṛḻā ca no adhi ca brūhi devādhā ca naḥ śarma yaccha dvibarhāḥ ||
english: Far from us be your cow-slaying and man-slaying, O ruler of heroes; let your favour be with us. Be gracious to us and speak well of us, O God, and give us doubly-woven shelter.

sanskrit: avocāma namo asmā avasyavaḥ śṛṇotu no havaṁ rudro marutvān | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: We who desire aid have spoken reverence to him; may Rudra with his Maruts hear our call. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: citraṁ devānāṁ ud agād anīkaṁ cakṣur mitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antariksaṁ sūrya ātmā jagatas tasthūṣaś ca ||
english: The wondrous face of the gods has arisen — the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. He has filled heaven, earth, and the mid-air; the Sun is the soul of all that moves and stands.

sanskrit: sūryo devīm uṣasaṁ rocamānāṁ maryo na yoṣām abhy eti paścāt | yatrā naro devayanto yugāni vitanvate prati bhadrāya bhadram ||
english: The Sun approaches the shining divine Uṣas from behind, as a young man follows a woman. Where men, devout in their worship, spread out the ages, setting the auspicious against the auspicious.

sanskrit: bhadrā aśvā haritaḥ sūryasya citrā etagvā anumādyāsaḥ | namasyanto diva ā pṛṣṭham asthuḥ pari dyāvāpṛthivī yanti sadyaḥ ||
english: Auspicious are the golden horses of the Sun, wondrous and diverse, worthy of praise. Reverently they have mounted to the back of heaven; they circle heaven and earth in a single day.

sanskrit: tat sūryasya devatvaṁ tan mahitvaṁ madhyā kartor vitataṁ saṁ jabhāra | yaded ayukta haritaḥ sadhasthād ād rātrī vāsas tanute simasmai ||
english: This is the divinity and this the greatness of the Sun — that in the midst of his course he drew in the stretched expanse. When he has unharnessed his golden horses from their station, at once Night draws her garment over all.

sanskrit: tan mitrasya varuṇasyābhicakṣe sūryo rūpaṁ kṛṇute dyor upasthe | anantam anyad ruśad asya pājaḥ kṛṣṇam anyad dharitaḥ saṁ bharanti ||
english: For Mitra and Varuṇa to behold, the Sun manifests his form in heaven's lap. One of his bright rays extends without end; the golden horses carry away the other, the dark one.

sanskrit: adyā devā uditā sūryasya nir aṁhasaḥ pipṛtā nir avadyāt | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Today, O gods, at the rising of the Sun, deliver us from sin and free us from reproach. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that blessing.

sanskrit: nāsatyābhyām barhir iva pra vṛñje stomāṁ iyarmy abhriyeva vātaḥ | yāv arbhagāya vimadāya jāyāṁ senājuvā nyūhathū rathena ||
english: I press out hymns to the two Nāsatyas as one strews the sacred grass, as wind drives the cloud. You two who carried the bride to young Vimada on your chariot swift as the army's vanguard.

sanskrit: vīḷupatmabhir āśuhemabhir vā devānāṁ vā jūtibhiḥ śāśadānā | tad rāsabho nāsatyā sahasram ājā yamasya pradhane jigāya ||
english: Whether by swift-rushing, firm-flying courses, or by the impulse of the gods, ever-triumphant — the ass won that thousand for you, O Nāsatyas, in the contest at the race of Yama.

sanskrit: tugro ha bhujyum aśvinodameghe rayiṁ na kaś cin mamṛvāṁ avāhāḥ | tam ūhathu naubhir ātmanvatībhir antarikṣaprūdbhir apodakābhiḥ ||
english: Tugra had dispatched Bhujyu into the cloud-ocean, as one sends away one who might die — without finding riches. You two carried him back in self-moving ships that filled the air, that did not founder in water.

sanskrit: tisraḥ kṣapas trir ahātitvrajatdbhir nāsatyā bhujyum ūhathuḥ pataṁgaiḥ | samudrasya dhanvann ārdrasyā pāre tribhī rathai śatapadbhiḥ ṣaḷaśvaiḥ ||
english: For three nights and three days, O Nāsatyas, you carried Bhujyu in flying boats, over the far shore of the watery desert sea, with three hundred-footed, six-horsed chariots.

sanskrit: anārambhaṇe tad avīrayethām anāsthāne agrabhaṇe samudre | yad aśvinā ūhathu bhujyum astaṁ śatāritrāṁ nāvam ātasthivāṁsam ||
english: You displayed your heroism in that ocean without footing, without resting place, without holding — when, O Aśvins, you carried Bhujyu home in a ship with a hundred oars.

sanskrit: yam aśvinā dadathuḥ śvetam aśvam aghāśvāya śaśvad it svasti | tad vāṁ dātram mahi kīrtenyam bhūt paidvo vājī sadam id dhavyo aryaḥ ||
english: The white horse which you two gave to Pedu, the son of Agha — ever for his welfare — that gift of yours is great and praiseworthy. The steed of Pedu, the victor, is always to be invoked by the noble.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ narā stuvate pajriyāya kakṣīvate aradataṁ puraṁdhim | kārotarāc chaphād aśvasya vṛṣṇaḥ śataṁ kumbhām asiñcataṁ surāyāḥ ||
english: For Kakṣīvant the Pajriya who praises you, O men, you both gave forth wisdom. From the hoof of the victorious horse you poured a hundred jars of liquor.

sanskrit: himenāgniṁ ghraṁsam avārayethāṁ pitumatīm ūrjam asmā adhattam | ṛbīse atriṁ aśvinā vanitam un ninyathuḥ sarvagaṇaṁ svasti ||
english: You two shielded Agni from the cold heat of frost and bestowed on him food with nourishment. You rescued Atri from the pit, O Aśvins, and raised him up with all his people in safety.

sanskrit: parāvataṁ nāsatyānudethām uccābudhnaṁ cakrathur jihmabāram | kṣarann āpo na pāyanāya rāye sahasrāya tṛṣyate gotamasya ||
english: You two pursued the far-off Nāsatyas; you made the watering-trough with its high bottom and slanting edge. Like flowing waters, you poured forth a thousand gifts of cattle for Gotama who thirsted.

sanskrit: jujuruṣo nāsatyo uta vavrim prāmuñcataṁ drāpim iva cyavānāt | prātirataṁ jahitasyāyur dasrād it patiṁ akṛṇutaṁ kanīnām ||
english: O Nāsatyas, you stripped from the ageing Cyavāna his worn-out garment as one removes a robe, and extended his life that had been abandoned. You marvellous ones made him the husband of maidens.

sanskrit: tad vāṁ narā śaṁsyaṁ rādhyaṁ cābhiṣtiman nāsatyā varūtham | yad vidvāṁsā nidhim ivāpagūḷham ud darśatād ūpathur vandanāya ||
english: That, O Nāsatyas, was a praiseworthy and successful act of protection that you performed — when you, with full knowledge, like one unearthing a hidden treasure, raised Vandana up to a sight of beauty.

sanskrit: tad vāṁ narā sanaye daṁsa ugram āviṣ kṛṇomi tanyatur na vṛṣṭim | dadyaṅ ha yan madhv ātharvaṇo vām aśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yad īm uvāca ||
english: That wonderful deed of yours, O men, for the winning of prizes, I make manifest like thunder that brings rain. When Dadhyaṅc Ātharvaṇa told you about the Soma nectar through the head of a horse.

sanskrit: ajohavīn nāsatyā karā vām mahe yāman purubhujā puraṁdhiḥ | śrutaṁ tac chāsur iva vadhrīmatyā hiraṇyahastam aśvināv adattam ||
english: The bountiful, wise Vadhrīmatī called to you, O Nāsatyas, on a great journey, O much-favouring ones. You heard — as at the bidding of a teacher — and gave her a golden-handed son, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: āsno vṛkasya vartikām abhīke yuvaṁ narā nāsatyā amumuktam | uto kavim purubhujā yuvaṁ ha kṛpamāṇam akṛṇutaṁ vicakṣe ||
english: You two, O men, O Nāsatyas, freed the quail from the very jaws of the wolf in the encounter. And you made the seer who was weeping, O much-favouring ones, able to see again.

sanskrit: caritram hi ver ivācchedi parṇam ājā khelas ya paritakmyāyām | sadyo jaṅghām āyasīṁ viśpalāyai dhane hite sartave praty adhattam ||
english: For the wing of a bird, like a leaf, was cut off in the battle at the time of Khelā's deadly contest. Instantly you fitted Viśpalā with an iron leg, so she could run when the prize was set.

sanskrit: śataṁ meṣān vṛkye cakṣadānam ṛjrāśvaṁ taṁ pitāndhaṁ cakāra | tasmā akṣī nāsatyā vicakṣa ādha ttaṁ dasrā bhiṣajāv anarvan ||
english: His father blinded Ṛjrāśva who had given a hundred rams to a she-wolf. To him, O Nāsatyas, O wondrous healers, you gave eyes to see clearly, you who are unharmed.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ rathaṁ duhitā sūryasya kārṣmevātiṣṭhad arvatā jayantī | viśve devā anv amanyanta hṛdbhiḥ sam u śriyā nāsatyā sacethe ||
english: The daughter of the Sun mounted your chariot conquering, like a cloth spread over it. All the gods agreed with their hearts; and you, O Nāsatyas, are joined together with beauty.

sanskrit: yad ayātaṁ divodāsāya vartir bharadvājāyāśvinā hayantā | revad uvāha sacano ratho vāṁ vṛṣabhaś ca śiṁśumāraś ca yuktā ||
english: When you two came bringing aid to Divodāsa and Bharadvāja, O swift-going Aśvins — your friendly chariot bore much wealth, with a bull and a dolphin yoked to it.

sanskrit: rayiṁ sukṣatraṁ svapAtyam āyuḥ suvīryaṁ nāsatyā vahantā | ā jahnāvīṁ samanasopa vājais trir ahno bhāgaṁ dadhatīm ayātam ||
english: Bearing wealth, good lordship, long life, and heroic might, O Nāsatyas — you came to the Jahnāvī river with prizes, as she who receives her share three times daily, with harmonious mind.

sanskrit: parivṣtaṁ jāhuṣaṁ viśvataḥ sīṁ sugebhir naktam ūhathū rajobhiḥ | vibhindunā nāsatyā rathena vi parvatāṁ ajarayū ayātam ||
english: You carried Jāhūṣa, hemmed in on all sides, through the night by easy passages across the dust-clouds. With the Vibhindhu chariot, O ever-youthful Nāsatyas, you cleft the mountains as you went.

sanskrit: ekasyā vastor āvataṁ raṇāya vaśam aśvinā sanaye sahasrā | nir ahataṁ ducchunā indravantā pṛthuśravaso vṛṣaṇāv arātīḥ ||
english: In a single day, O Aśvins, you came to help Vaśa win a thousand in the prize contest. You two mighty ones, allied with Indra, drove away misfortune from the far-famed Pṛthuśravas.

sanskrit: śarasya cid ārcatkasyāvatād ā nīcād uccā cakrathuḥ pātave vāḥ | śayave cin nāsatyā śacībhis jasurayā staryam pipyathu gām ||
english: From the stalk of the reed Ārcat you two drew water upward from below to drink. For Śaya who was wasting away, O Nāsatyas, you made the barren cow give milk with your powers.

sanskrit: avasyate stuvate kṛṣṇiyāya ṛjūyate nāsatyā śacībhiḥ | paśuṁ na naṣṭam iva darśanāya viṣṇāpvaṁ dadathur viśvakāya ||
english: For Kṛṣṇiya who seeks protection, who praises, who prays sincerely, O Nāsatyas, with your powers — like a lost animal found again — you gave Viṣṇāpū to Viśvaka for his sight.

sanskrit: daśa rātrīr aśivenā nava dyūn avanaddhama śnathitam apsu antaḥ | viprutaṁ rebham udani pravṛktam un ninyathuḥ somam iva sraveṇa ||
english: For ten nights and nine days, bound and battered, submerged within the waters, you raised up Rebha, scattered and buried in the water, as one draws out Soma through a strainer.

sanskrit: pra vāṁ daṁsāṁsy aśvinā avocam asya patiḥ syāṁ sugavaḥ suvīraḥ | uta paśyann aśnuvan dīrgham āyur astam ivej jarimāṇaṁ jagamyām ||
english: I have declared your wondrous deeds, O Aśvins; may I be the master of good cattle and good heroes. Seeing and enjoying long life, may I reach old age like a home to be reached.

sanskrit: madhvaḥ somasyāśvinā madāya pratno hotā vivāsate vām | barhiṣmatī rātir viśritā gīr iṣā yātaṁ nāsatyopa vājaiḥ ||
english: The ancient Hotṛ seeks to win you two, O Aśvins, for the joy of the sweet Soma. The gift is rich in sacred grass and the hymn is released — come, O Nāsatyas, with prizes and food.

sanskrit: yo vām aśvinā manaso javīyān rathaḥ svaśvo viśa ā jigāti | yena gacchathaḥ sukṛto duroṇaṁ tena narā vartir asmabhyaṁ yātam ||
english: That chariot of yours, O Aśvins, swifter than mind, with good horses, that comes to the clans — with which you go to the house of the pious worshipper — come to us on that path, O men.

sanskrit: ṛṣiṁ narāv aṁhasaḥ pāñcajanyam ṛbīsād atriṁ muñcatho gaṇena | minantā dasyor aśivasya māyā anupūrvaṁ vṛṣaṇā codayantā ||
english: You two, O men, freed the seer Atri who belongs to five peoples from the pit of distress. Destroying the wiles of the wicked Dasyu, you mighty ones urged him on in proper order.

sanskrit: aśvaṁ na gūḷham aśvinā durevaḥ ṛṣiṁ narā vṛṣaṇā rebham apsu | saṁ taṁ riṇītho viprutaṁ daṁsobhir na vāṁ jūryanti pūrvyā kṛtāni ||
english: Like a horse hidden in a bad place, O Aśvins, O mighty men, the seer Rebha was buried in the waters; you released him, scattered as he was, with your wonders. Your ancient deeds do not grow old.

sanskrit: suṣupvāṁsaṁ na nirṛter upasthe sūryaṁ na dasrā tamasi kṣiyantam | śubhe rukmaṁ na darśataṁ nikhātam ud ūpathu aśvinā vandanāya ||
english: Like one deeply sleeping in the lap of destruction, like the sun dwelling in darkness, O wondrous ones — like a gleaming ornament buried and hidden for adornment — you raised up Vandana, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: tad vāṁ narā śaṁsyam pajriyeṇa kakṣīvatā nāsatyā parijman | śaphād aśvasya vājino janāya śataṁ kumbhāṁ asiñcatam madhūnām ||
english: That, O Nāsatyas, O all-surrounding ones, is your praiseworthy deed — with Kakṣīvant the Pajriya — when from the hoof of the victorious horse you poured for the people a hundred jars of honey.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ narā stuvate kṛṣṇiyāya viṣṇāpvaṁ dadathur viśvakāya | ghoṣāyai cit pitṛṣade duroṇe patiṁ jūryantyā aśvinā adattam ||
english: You two, O men, gave Viṣṇāpu to Viśvaka who was praising you for Kṛṣṇiya. Even for Ghoṣā sitting in her father's house, to her who was growing old, O Aśvins, you gave a husband.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ śyāvāya ruśatīm adattam mahaḥ kṣoṇasyāśvinā kaṇvāya | pravācyaṁ tad vṛṣaṇā kṛtaṁ vāṁ yan nārṣadāya śravo adhy adhattam ||
english: You gave the bright one to dark Śyāva, O Aśvins, and the great earthy one to Kaṇva. That deed of yours, O mighty ones, is worthy to be proclaimed — how you bestowed fame upon Nārṣada.

sanskrit: purū varpāṁsy aśvinā dadhānā ni pedave ūhathur āśum aśvam | sahasrasāṁ vājinam apratītam ahihanam śravasyaṁ tarutram ||
english: Assuming many forms, O Aśvins, you brought the swift horse to Pedu — the prize-winner of a thousand, unvanquished, the serpent-slayer, glorious, the conqueror.

sanskrit: etāni vāṁ śravasyā sudānū brahmāṅgūṣaṁ sadanaṁ rodasyoḥ | yad vām pajrāso aśvinā havante yātam iṣā ca viduṣe ca vājam ||
english: These deeds of yours, O bounteous ones, are the praise-worthy abode of hymns for both worlds. When the Pajriya people call upon you two, O Aśvins — come with food and prizes to the knower.

sanskrit: sūnor mānenāśvinā gṛṇānā vājaṁ viprāya bhuraṇā radantā | agastye brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānā saṁ viśpalāṁ nāsatyāriṇītam ||
english: Praised with the prayer of a son, O Aśvins, you who sustain the inspired seer and grant him the prize — swelling with the prayer of Agastya, O Nāsatyas, you restored Viśpalā.

sanskrit: kuha yāntā suṣṭutiṁ kāvyasya divo napātā vṛṣaṇā śayutrā | hiraṇyasyeva kalaśaṁ nikhātam ud ūpathu daśame aśvinā ahan ||
english: Going where to receive the excellent praise of the poet, O sons of heaven, O mighty ones, O youthful ones? Like a golden pot buried underground you raised him up — on the tenth day, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ cyavānam aśvinā jarantaṁ punar yuvānaṁ cakrathuḥ śacībhiḥ | yuvo rathaṁ duhitā sūryasya saha śriyā nāsatyāvṛṇīta ||
english: You two, O Aśvins, made the ageing Cyavāna young again with your powers. The daughter of the Sun chose your chariot, O Nāsatyas, together with its beauty.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ tugrāya pūrvyebhir evaiḥ punarManyāv abhavataṁ yuvānā | yuvam bhujyum arṇaso niḥ samudrād vibhir ūhathur ṛjrebhir aśvaiḥ ||
english: You two, with your ancient ways, became like new-spirited youths for Tugra again. You carried Bhujyu out of the ocean with your swift-flying, straight-dashing horses.

sanskrit: ajohavīd aśvinā taugryo vāṁ proḷhaḥ samudram avyathir jagaMvān | niṣ ṭam ūhathuḥ suyujā rathena manojasavā vṛṣaṇā svasti ||
english: The son of Tugra called to you two, O Aśvins, as he was cast into the ocean, unshaken though he had gone in. You carried him out in your well-yoked chariot, swift as thought, O mighty ones, in safety.

sanskrit: ajohavīd aśvinā vartikā vām āsno yat sīm amuñcataṁ vṛkasya | vi jayuṣā yayathuḥ sānv adrer jātaṁ viṣvāco ahataṁ viṣeṇa ||
english: The quail called out to you two, O Aśvins, when you freed her from the very mouth of the wolf. You went victoriously over the mountain ridge and struck down the newborn Viṣvāc with poison.

sanskrit: śataṁ meṣān vṛkye māmahānaṁ tamaḥ praṇītam aśivena pitrā | ākṣī ṛjrāśve aśvinā adhattaṁ jyotir andhāya cakrathur vicakṣe ||
english: Ṛjrāśva, who had given a hundred rams to the she-wolf, was led into darkness by his wicked father. You two, O Aśvins, placed eyes in Ṛjrāśva; you made light for the blind so he could see clearly.

sanskrit: śunam andhāya bharaṁ ahvayat sā vṛkīr aśvinā vṛṣaṇā nareti | jāraḥ kanīna iva cakṣadāna ṛjrāśvaḥ śataṁ ekaṁ ca meṣān ||
english: She-wolf called out to you, O mighty Aśvins, O men, carrying welfare for the blind: 'A lover like a youth, giving freely, Ṛjrāśva gave a hundred and one rams.'

sanskrit: mahī vāṁ ūtir aśvinā mayobhūr uta srāmaṁ dhiṣṇyā saṁ riṇīthaḥ | athā yuvām id ahvayat puraṁdhir āgacchatam sīṁ vṛṣaṇāv avobhiḥ ||
english: Great and bringing joy is your aid, O Aśvins; O wise ones, you heal even the paralysed. And so the wise one called upon you both; come to her, O mighty ones, with your aids.

sanskrit: adhenuṁ dasrā staryaṁ viṣaktām apinvataṁ śayave aśvinā gām | yuvaṁ śacībhir vimadāya jāyaṁ ny ūhathuḥ purumitrasya yoṣām ||
english: You caused the barren, dry, infertile cow to give milk for Śaya, O wondrous Aśvins. With your powers you carried the woman of Purumitra as wife to Vimada.

sanskrit: yavaṁ vṛkeṇāśvinā vapanteṣaṁ duhantā manuṣāya dasrā | abhi dasyum bakureṇā dhamanto uru jyotiś cakrathur āryāya ||
english: Sowing barley with the plough, milking food for mankind, O wondrous Aśvins — blowing the Dasyu away with a pipe, you made broad light for the Ārya.

sanskrit: ātharvaṇāyāśvinā dadhīce aśvyaṁ śiraḥ praty airayatam | sa vāṁ madhu pra vocad ṛtāyan tvāṣṭraṁ yad dasrāv apikakṣyaṁ vām ||
english: You set on Dadhīca Ātharvaṇa an equine head, O Aśvins. Walking in truth, he told you the sweet nectar — that Tvāṣṭra mystery which is your secret, O wondrous ones.

sanskrit: sadā kavī sumatiṁ ā cake vāṁ viśvā dhiyo aśvinā prāvatam me | asme rayiṁ nāsatyā bṛhantam apatyasācaṁ śrutyaṁ rarāthām ||
english: I always, as a sage, have sought your kindness; O Aśvins, favour all my prayers. Bestow on us, O Nāsatyas, great wealth accompanied by offspring and worthy of being heard of.

sanskrit: hiraṇyahastam aśvinā rarāṇā putraṁ narā vadhrīmatyā adattam | tridhā ha śyāvam aśvinā vikastam uj jīvasai airayataṁ sudānū ||
english: You two, O men, O bounteous Aśvins, delighting, gave a golden-handed son to Vadhrīmatī. You set Śyāva who was split in three parts upright and alive again.

sanskrit: etāni vām aśvinā vīryāṇi pra pūrvyāṇy āyavo 'vocan | brahma kṛṇvanto vṛṣaṇā yuvabhyāṁ suvīrāso vidathaṁ ā vadema ||
english: These heroic deeds of yours, O Aśvins, the people have proclaimed, the ancient deeds. O mighty ones, forming the prayer for you both, may we, with good heroes, speak our wisdom at the assembly.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ ratho aśvinā śyenapatvā sumṛḻīkaḥ svavāṁ yātv arvāṅ | yo martyasya manaso javīyān trivandhu ro vṛṣaṇā vātaraṁhāḥ ||
english: Let your chariot come to us, O Aśvins, that flies like a hawk, that is gracious, that carries good things — that chariot which is swifter than a mortal's thought, three-seated, O mighty ones, that races like the wind.

sanskrit: trivandhu reṇa trivṛtā rathena tricakreṇa suvṛtā yātam arvāk | pinvataṁ gā jinvataṁ arvato no vardha yataṁ aśvinā vīram asme ||
english: Come to us in the three-seated, triple, three-wheeled chariot, rolling well. Swell our cows, quicken our horses, O Aśvins, and increase the hero among us.

sanskrit: pravadyāmanā suvṛtā rathena dasrāv imaṁ śṛṇutaṁ ślokam adreḥ | kim aṅga vāṁ praty avartiṁ gamiṣṭhā hur viprāso aśvinā purājāḥ ||
english: Moving forward with your well-rolling chariot, O wondrous ones, hear this praise from the pressing stone. What offering, O Aśvins, do the inspired sages of old name as most fitting to win you back?

sanskrit: ā vāṁ śyenāso aśvinā vahantu rathe yuktāsa āśavaḥ pataṁgāḥ | ye apturo divyāso na gṛdhrā abhi prayo nāsatyā vahanti ||
english: May your hawks carry you, O Aśvins — swift flying ones harnessed to your chariot — those that are airborne like heavenly vultures, that carry food to you, O Nāsatyas.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ rathaṁ yuvatis tiṣṭhad atra juṣṭvī narā duhitā sūryasya | pari vām aśvā vapuṣaḥ pataṁgā vayo vahanty aruṣā abhīke ||
english: A young woman mounts your chariot here, having been welcomed, O men — the daughter of the Sun. Your beautiful, bird-like, reddish horses carry you in the encounter.

sanskrit: ud vandanam airataṁ daṁsanābhir ud rebhaṁ dasrā vṛṣaṇā śacībhiḥ | niṣ ṭaugriyam pārayathaḥ samudrāt punaś cyavānaṁ cakrathur yuvānam ||
english: You raised up Vandana with your wonders; you raised up Rebha, O wondrous ones, O mighty ones, with your powers. You bore the son of Tugra across the ocean; you made Cyavāna young again.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ atraye 'vanītāya taptam ūrjam omānam aśvinā adhattam | yuvaṁ kaṇvāyāpiriptāya cakṣuḥ praty adhattaṁ suṣṭutiṁ juṣāṇā ||
english: You placed warm nourishment and shelter for Atri who had fallen in distress, O Aśvins. And you, delighting in fair praise, restored sight to Kaṇva who had been robbed of it.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ dhenuṁ śayave nādhitāyāpinvatam aśvinā pūrvyāya | amuñcataṁ vartikāṁ aṁhaso niḥ prati jaṅghāṁ viśpalāyā adhattam ||
english: You filled with milk the cow for Śaya the ancient needy one, O Aśvins. You freed the quail from distress, and fitted Viśpalā's leg.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ śvetaṁ pedave indrajūtam ahihanam aśvinādattam aśvam | johūtram aryo abhibhūtiṁ ugraṁ sahasrasāṁ vṛṣaṇaṁ vīḍvaṅgam ||
english: You two, O Aśvins, gave the white horse to Pedu — urged by Indra, serpent-slayer — the ever-invoked, the lord's, the mightily conquering, the prize-winner of thousands, the mighty-limbed bull.

sanskrit: tā vāṁ narā sv avase sujātā havāmahe aśvinā nādhamānāḥ | ā na upa vasumātā rathena giro juṣāṇā suvitāya yātam ||
english: You, O well-born men, O Aśvins, we call for our own protection, imploring you. Come to us near in your wealth-bearing chariot, delighting in hymns, for our well-being.

sanskrit: ā śyenasya javasā nūtanenāsme yātaṁ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | have hi vām aśvinā rātahavyaḥ śaśvattamāyā uṣaso vyuṣṭau ||
english: Come to us with the new speed of a hawk, in unison, O Nāsatyas. For the one who pours oblation calls upon you, O Aśvins, ever and ever at the shining forth of Dawn.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ ratham purumāyam manojuvaṁ jīrāśvaṁ yajñiyaṁ jīvase huve | sahasraketuṁ vaninaṁ śatadvasuṁ śruṣṭīvānaṁ varivod hām abhi prayaḥ ||
english: I call your chariot hither, O Aśvins, for our life — full of wonders, swift as thought, with spirited horses, worthy of worship; thousand-bannered, laden with wood, with a hundred treasures, prompt to hear, space-giving, to this libation.

sanskrit: ūrdhvā dhītiḥ praty asya prayāmany adhāyi śasman sam ayanta ā diśaḥ | svādāmi gharmaṁ prati yanty ūtaya ā vām ūrjānī ratham aśvinā ruhat ||
english: Upright is the prayer at the going of this one; it was laid down in the chanting; the directions came together. The aids come sweetening the warm drink — the Ūrjānī woman has mounted your chariot, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: saṁ yan mithaḥ paspṛdhānāso agmata śubhe makhā amitā jāyavo raṇe | yuvor aha pravanecekite ratho yad aśvinā vahathaḥ sūriṁ ā varam ||
english: When the contestants, striving against each other, came together in the contest, the exuberant, uncounted, swift ones shone for glory in battle. Your chariot is perceived going downhill, O Aśvins, as you carry the patron to the prize.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ bhujyum bhuramāṇaṁ vibhir gataṁ svayuktibhir nivahantā pitṛbhya ā | yāsiṣṭaṁ vartir vṛṣaṇā vijenyaṁ divodāsāya mahi ceti vām avaḥ ||
english: You two carried Bhujyu who was tossing in the waters, in self-impelled ships, bringing him back to his fathers. You two, O mighty ones, won the conquest — your greatness and your aid to Divodāsa is well known.

sanskrit: yuvor aśvinā vapuṣe yuvāyujaṁ rathaṁ vāṇī yematur asya śardham | ā vāṁ patitvam sakhyāya jagmuṣī yoṣāvṛṇīta jenyā yuvāṁ patī ||
english: The two women have guided your chariot, harnessed in youth for beauty, with its swift troop, O Aśvins. The maiden came seeking your friendship and companionship — she chose you two as her lords.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ rebham pariṣūter uruṣyatho himenā gharmaṁ paritaptam atraye | yuvaṁ śayor avasampipy athur gavi pra dīrgheṇa vandanas tāry āyuṣā ||
english: You two protect Rebha from distress, and the heat of frost searing Atri. You two filled the shelter of Śaya with a cow's milk — Vandana prolongs his life through a long span.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ vandanaṁ nirṛtaṁ jaraṇyayā rathaṁ na dasrā karaṇā sam invathaḥ | kṣetrād ā vipraṁ janatho vipanyayā pra vām atra vidhate daṁsanā bhuvat ||
english: You two, O wondrous ones, restore Vandana from ruin through your craftsmanship, as workmen restore a chariot. You bring the inspired one back from the field with your skill — let the wonders of you both, who are to be pleased, shine forth here.

sanskrit: agacchatāṁ kṛpamāṇam parāvati pituḥ svasya tyajasā nibādhitam | svarvatīr ita ūtīr yuvor aha citrā abhīke abhavann abhiṣṭayaḥ ||
english: You came to the weeping one in the distant land, hemmed in and abandoned by his own father. Your aids that carry sunlight and that come from here have become wondrous reliefs in the moment of encounter.

sanskrit: uta syā vāṁ madhu man makṣikārapa n made somasya auśijo huvanyati | yuvaṁ dadhīco mana ā vivāsatho athā śiraḥ prati vām aśvyaṁ vadat ||
english: And that sweet honey-dropping bee pours in the joy of Soma — the son of Uśij calls upon you. You two came to seek the mind of Dadhīca; and then the horse-head spoke your secret to you.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ pedave puruvāram aśvinā spṛdhāṁ śvetaṁ tarutāraṁ duvasyathaḥ | śaryair abhidyum pṛtanāsu duṣṭaraṁ carkṛtyam indram iva carṣaṇīsaham ||
english: You two honour Pedu with the manifold gift, O Aśvins — the white horse, the vanquisher of rivals. With his arrows he strikes the luminous one, unshakeable in battles — Indra-like, overpowering all men.

sanskrit: kā rādhad dhotrāśvinā vāṁ ko vāṁ joṣa ubhayoḥ | kathā vidhāty apracetāḥ ||
english: Who shall fulfil the priestly office for you two, O Aśvins? Who shall delight you both? How shall the unwitting one arrange this?

sanskrit: vidvāṁsāv id duraḥ pṛcched avidvān itthāparo acetāḥ | nū cin nu marte akrau ||
english: Only the knower should ask of the knowing two; the non-knower goes astray, ignorant. Now indeed has any mortal accomplished it?

sanskrit: tā vidvāṁsā havāmahe vāṁ tā no vidvāṁsā manma vocetam adya | prārcad dayamāno yuvākuḥ ||
english: Those two who know — we call upon you; those two who know — speak the prayer to us today. The one who longs for you called out, praising.

sanskrit: vi pṛcchāmi pākyā na devān vaṣaṭkṛtasyādbhutasya dasrā | pātaṁ ca sahyaso yuvaṁ ca rabhyaso naḥ ||
english: I ask like a simple one before the gods, O wondrous Aśvins, of the marvellous one for whom the vaṣaṭ-call is made. Protect us from what overcomes, and from what strikes us down.

sanskrit: pra yā ghoṣe bhṛgavāṇe na śobhe yayā vācā yajati pajriyo vām | praiṣayur na vidvān ||
english: That song shines forth like the roaring of a fire — with that voice the Pajriya worships you both. The knowing one has sent it forth as one dispatches a messenger.

sanskrit: śrutaṁ gāyatraṁ takavānasyāhaṁ cid dhi rerebhāśvinā vām | ākṣī śubhas patī dan ||
english: I have heard the Gāyatra song of Takvan; I too have been extolling you two, O Aśvins. The lords of beauty gave eyes to one.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ hy āstam maho ran yuvaṁ vā yan niratataṁsatam | tā no vasū sugopā syātam pātaṁ no vṛkād aghāyoḥ ||
english: For you two have rejoiced greatly in the home, or in whatever you have spread out together. Be our two good protectors full of treasure; guard us from the wicked, malicious wolf.

sanskrit: mā kasmai dhātam abhy amitrīṇe no mākutrā no gṛhebhyo dhenavo guḥ | stanābhujo aśiśvīḥ ||
english: Give us not over to any hostile one; let not the milk-cows be taken anywhere from our houses — the young calves that suck the udder.

sanskrit: duhīyan mitradhi taye yuvāku rāye ca no mimītaṁ vājavatyai | iṣe ca no mimītaṁ dhenumatyai ||
english: May the cow give milk for the gratification of Mitra, and you two, O eager ones, measure out to us prize-winning wealth and food rich in cattle.

sanskrit: aśvinor asanaṁ ratham anaśvaṁ vājinīvatoḥ | tenāham bhūri cākana ||
english: The horseless chariot of the two Aśvins, full of prizes — with that I have greatly desired many things.

sanskrit: ayaṁ samaha mā tanūhyāte janāṁ anu | somapeyaṁ sukho rathaḥ ||
english: This very man, spreading out, does not decay among the peoples — the chariot of Soma-drinking is a pleasant one.

sanskrit: adha svapnasya nir vide abhuñjataś ca revataḥ | ubhā tā basri naśyataḥ ||
english: Thus both sleep and the wealthy man who enjoys without giving are seen to perish — both of them pass away at dawn.
